svg.aria-label: Single wiring diagram of the whole aarti lights build. On the left an INMP441 I2S microphone connects to the ESP32: SD to GPIO32 driven by the microphone, WS to GPIO25 and SCK to GPIO33 driven by the ESP32, VDD to 3.3 volts, GND to ground, and the L slash R pin tied to that same ground to select the left channel. The ESP32 is powered from its own USB adapter above it. From the ESP32's right side, GPIO4 goes through a 470 ohm series resistor to the DIN pad of a 180 pixel WS2812B strip. A separate 5 volt 4 amp supply feeds the strip's plus 5V and GND pads directly over mains-wire offcuts, a 1000 microfarad capacitor sits across that pair with its striped leg to ground, and the ESP32's ground drops onto the same ground wire at a soldered junction, which is the common ground the whole circuit depends on.
svg.title: Aarti lights wiring, as built

The ESP32 is powered from its own USB adapter above it. From the ESP32's right side, GPIO4 goes through a 470 ohm series resistor to the DIN pad of a 180 pixel WS2812B strip. A separate 5 volt 4 amp supply feeds the strip's plus 5V and GND pads directly over mains-wire offcuts, a 1000 microfarad capacitor sits across that pair with its striped leg to ground, and the ESP32's ground drops onto the same ground wire at a soldered junction, which is the common ground the whole circuit depends on.
